stages.name: Independent peoples
stages.desc: Illyrians, Thracians and Indian kingdoms outside both empires

stages.name: Persian Empire
stages.desc: Ruled by the Great King and his satraps

stages.name: Macedon and its Greek allies
stages.desc: Philip's kingdom and, from 337, the Greek League of Corinth it leads

stages.name: At war with Macedon
stages.desc: Resisting or in revolt against Philip or Alexander

stages.name: Macedonian governors
stages.desc: Conquered lands under Macedonian generals and satraps

stages.name: Persian and local rulers
stages.desc: Conquered lands left to Persian nobles or local kings who submitted

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The kings of Cyprus's cities, subject to Persia after a failed revolt
Cyprus's kings bring their ships to Alexander at Tyre and keep their thrones

states.name: Israel
timeline: A Persian province; Judah is governed from Jerusalem by its high priests
The coast road passes to Alexander's governors

states.name: Palestine
timeline: A Persian province; Gaza guards the road to Egypt
Gaza resists for two months and is stormed

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Phoenician city-kingdoms under Persia; Sidon was sacked after revolting in the 340s
Byblos and Sidon submit; a new king is set up in Sidon
Tyre holds out for seven months and is stormed

states.name: Syria
timeline: The Persian satrapy 'Beyond the River'
After Issus, Parmenion takes Damascus and Darius' baggage train

states.name: Uzbekistan
timeline: Sogdiana, the far north-east of the Persian Empire
Spitamenes leads Sogdiana in revolt
After the fall of the Sogdian Rock, Macedonian garrisons hold the land

states.name: Tajikistan
timeline: The eastern valleys of Sogdiana
Revolt; Alexander founds Alexandria Eschate, 'the Farthest', on the Jaxartes
Held by Macedonian garrisons

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Upper Macedonia and Paeonia, on the northern edge of Philip's kingdom

states.name: Albania
timeline: Illyrian kingdoms, beaten by Philip but never conquered
The Illyrian kings Cleitus and Glaucias fight Alexander at Pelion
The Illyrians stay outside Alexander's empire

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Persian satrapies of Asia Minor; near Assos, Aristotle's friend Hermias rules a small realm
Hermias is seized by Persian agents and put to death
Philip besieges Perinthus and Byzantium, Greek cities on today's European shore
Philip's advance guard under Parmenion crosses into Asia
After the Granicus, Macedonian governors take over; Queen Ada rules Caria for Alexander
Gordium and the battle of Issus

states.name: Greece
timeline: Philip's Macedon (Pella, Mieza, Aegae) rules the north with Thessaly and Epirus as allies; Athens, Thebes and Sparta are still free
Athens and Thebes ally against Philip
Chaeronea: Philip crushes Athens and Thebes; Alexander, eighteen, commands a wing
The Greek states, Sparta apart, join the League of Corinth under Macedon's lead
Thebes revolts and Alexander destroys it
Antipater holds Macedon and watches the Greeks while Alexander is in Asia
King Agis of Sparta rises and is defeated at Megalopolis (331 or 330)
News of Alexander's death: Athens leads the Lamian War against Macedon

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Babylonia and Assyria, the heart of the Persian Empire
After Gaugamela, Babylon opens its gates; the Persian Mazaeus stays as governor
At Opis, Alexander prays for concord between Macedonians and Persians
Alexander dies at Babylon

states.name: Iran
timeline: Persis, Media and Susiana: the Persian homeland
Susa surrenders; its Persian governor Abulites keeps his post
Persepolis is burned; Darius is killed by his own nobles
Back from India, Alexander executes several governors; mass weddings at Susa

states.name: Pakistan
timeline: Indian kingdoms of the Indus; Persian rule here had faded
Alexander fights his way down the Swat valley and takes the rock of Aornos
King Taxiles and King Porus keep their kingdoms as Alexander's allies
The Malli resist; Alexander is gravely wounded
The Indus lands are left to Porus, Taxiles and a few Macedonian officers

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: Thracian kingdoms of the Odrysians
Philip campaigns in Thrace, 342–340
Thrace becomes a Macedonian province; Philippopolis is founded
Alexander fights the Triballi and crosses the Danube
Thrace is held for Macedon by a general

states.name: Kuwait
timeline: The coast of Babylonia
Passes to Alexander with Babylonia

states.name: Afghanistan
timeline: Bactria, Aria and Arachosia, the empire's eastern satrapies
Alexander keeps or names Persian governors
Bactria and Sogdiana rise under Spitamenes
Macedonian governors and garrisons hold Bactria; Alexander marries Roxane

states.name: Turkmenistan
timeline: Parthia and Margiana, Persian satrapies
Phrataphernes, a Persian noble, governs Parthia for Alexander

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Persian lands east of the Jordan
Passes to Alexander with Syria

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Artaxerxes III reconquers Egypt and ends its last native dynasty (343/2)
The Persian satrap surrenders; Alexander is received as pharaoh
Alexandria is founded; Macedonians command the garrisons

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: The kings of Cyprus's cities, subject to Persia after a failed revolt
Cyprus's kings bring their ships to Alexander at Tyre and keep their thrones

states.name: Cyprus U.N. Buffer Zone
timeline: The kings of Cyprus's cities, subject to Persia after a failed revolt
Cyprus's kings bring their ships to Alexander at Tyre and keep their thrones

events.title: Aristotle summoned
events.text: Philip II sends for Aristotle, about forty-one, to teach his thirteen-year-old son Alexander.

events.title: School at Mieza
events.text: Lessons in the sanctuary of the Nymphs near Mieza, where Plutarch says Aristotle's stone seats were still shown.

events.title: Stagira restored
events.text: Plutarch says Philip's fee was to rebuild Aristotle's home town, which he had destroyed.

events.title: Egypt reconquered
events.text: Artaxerxes III retakes Egypt, ending the last native dynasty of pharaohs.

events.title: Philip in Thrace
events.text: Philip conquers the Thracian kingdoms and founds Philippopolis, today's Plovdiv.

events.title: Hermias betrayed
events.text: Aristotle's friend and patron Hermias of Atarneus is seized by the Persians and executed.

events.title: Alexander regent
events.text: At sixteen, Alexander governs Macedon while Philip makes war in the east.

events.title: Siege of Byzantium
events.text: Philip besieges Perinthus and Byzantium and fails to take them.

events.title: Chaeronea
events.text: Philip defeats Athens and Thebes; Alexander, eighteen, commands a wing.

events.title: League of Corinth
events.text: The Greek states swear alliance under Philip's leadership for a war on Persia.

events.title: Philip murdered
events.text: Philip is stabbed to death in the theatre at Aegae; Alexander, twenty, is king.

events.title: Darius III
events.text: Darius III becomes Great King of Persia.

events.title: Across the Danube
events.text: Alexander beats the Triballi and crosses the Danube against the Getae.

events.title: Pelion
events.text: Alexander breaks out of a trap set by the Illyrian kings.

events.title: Thebes destroyed
events.text: Thebes revolts; Alexander razes the city and sells its people into slavery.

events.title: The Lyceum
events.text: Aristotle returns to Athens and opens his own school at the Lyceum.

events.title: Tomb of Achilles
events.text: At Troy, Alexander honours the tomb of Achilles, the hero of the Iliad.

events.title: The Granicus
events.text: Alexander's first victory over the Persian satraps.

events.title: Halicarnassus
events.text: After a siege, Alexander leaves Caria to its queen, Ada.

events.title: Gordium
events.text: Alexander cuts, or unties, the Gordian knot.

events.title: Battle of Issus
events.text: Darius flees; his family and his treasures, among them a precious casket, are captured.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: The island city holds out for seven months before it is stormed.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Gaza resists for two months; Alexander is wounded.

events.title: Alexandria
events.text: Alexander founds Alexandria on the coast of Egypt.

events.title: Oracle of Siwa
events.text: In the desert, the oracle of Ammon greets Alexander as a son of the god.

events.title: Gaugamela
events.text: Alexander defeats Darius' great army on 1 October.

events.title: Babylon
events.text: Babylon opens its gates; the Persian Mazaeus stays on as governor.

events.title: Persepolis burned
events.text: Alexander burns the palaces of the Persian kings.

events.title: Darius killed
events.text: Darius is murdered by his own nobles as Alexander closes in.

events.title: Alexandria Eschate
events.text: On the Jaxartes, Alexander founds 'Alexandria the Farthest'.

events.title: Cleitus killed
events.text: At Maracanda, Alexander kills his friend Cleitus in a drunken quarrel.

events.title: Marriage to Roxane
events.text: Alexander marries Roxane, daughter of a Bactrian noble.

events.title: The bow refused
events.text: Callisthenes refuses to bow down to Alexander in the Persian manner.

events.title: Callisthenes arrested
events.text: After the pages' plot, Callisthenes is accused and dies in custody.

events.title: The Hydaspes
events.text: Alexander defeats King Porus, then leaves him his kingdom.

events.title: The Hyphasis
events.text: On the Beas, the army refuses to march farther east.

events.title: Among the Malli
events.text: Leaping alone inside a town's wall, Alexander is gravely wounded.

events.title: Gedrosian desert
events.text: The march home through the desert costs many lives.

events.title: Weddings at Susa
events.text: Alexander and some eighty companions marry Persian noblewomen.

events.title: Opis
events.text: Alexander prays for concord between Macedonians and Persians.

events.title: Death in Babylon
events.text: Alexander dies of a fever in June, aged thirty-two.

events.title: Lamian War
events.text: Athens leads the Greeks against Macedon.

events.title: Aristotle leaves
events.text: Charged with impiety, Aristotle withdraws to Chalcis, where he dies in 322.

metrics.label: Left to Persian and local rulers

chartNote: Share of the area of 22 modern countries, from Albania to Pakistan, by who ruled there each year. Regions are today's boundaries and each country takes its dominant status: Greece holds both Macedon's heartland and the free Greek cities, and Alexander's march east of the Indus, into today's India, is shown only by events. A deliberate simplification.
